title: Pilot Sentinel Ops Cookbook (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a light-weight, actionable playbook for running small "pilot-sentinel" canaries and A/B pilots across teams. The sentinel is a dedicated micro-cohort + steward workflow intended to detect regressions early while minimizing customer impact and cost.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Deploy a pilot-sentinel for any rollout where model behavior or cost profile can materially change user experience or unit economics.
- Use shadow/mirror sampling for risky behavior checks, time-decay aggregated signals for early detection, and a rotating micro-steward roster for human-in-the-loop judgment.
- Automated throttles + human confirmation for rollback. If automated thresholds fire and steward cannot validate within 10m, execute fallback.

Scope / When to use:
- New model family or quantized variant with unknown hallucination or latency impacts.
- Changes to routing that affect backend model mix (e.g., routing cheaper variant for edge cases).
- High-cost experiments (expected >10% cost delta) where economic signal must be gated.

Sentinel patterns (choose one):
- Shadow (best for safety/behaviors): replicate requests to new variant, log responses, surface divergences to stewards. No user-visible change.
- Mirror-sample (best for latency/cost): route 2–5% mirrored traffic with throttling and token budget cap. Use for perf/cost checks with limited exposure.
- Live A/B (best for product metrics): direct small cohort (0.5–2%) traffic split, with feature-flagged rollback. Only for low-safety-risk changes.

Roles & rotation:
- Micro-Steward (primary): rotates daily from product/observability/solutions-eng. First responder for signal alerts; owns quick triage.
- Observability Lead (secondary): verifies metric validity and instrumentation, owns metric dashboards.
- Deployment Owner: the engineer who triggered rollout; must be reachable for hotfixes.
- Exec Gate (if >10% cost change or high-visibility): product lead or oncall manager.

Micro-Steward rotation protocol:
- Roster of 6 people per fortnight. Each steward 24h duty window (08:00–08:00 PT) with 2 backups.
- Steward responsibility: check the sentinel dashboard upon shift start, validate any queued anomalies, and run the quick-sample queries below if alerts exist.
- Handoff notes: steward adds 3-line summary to the shift doc in the sentinel channel and tags next steward.

Signal matrix (unweighted list):
- Latency (p50, p95, p99) — metric: inference.latency.ms, trace: span=runtime/infer
- Error rate (5xx / internal errors) — metric: inference.errors.total
- Token growth / cost delta — metric: inference.tokens.per-request, billing.delta_pct
- Behavioral drift (semantic divergence / hallucination score) — metric: sanity.hallucination_score (see evaluation harness)
- Quality regressions (NPS-like proxies, rerank F1, LLM-answer pass rate) — custom eval suite tied to prompt set
- Upstream resource saturation (GPU queue depth, mem pressure) — infra.gpu.queue_depth, infra.gpu.mem_pct

Aggregation policy (time-decay):
- Compute both instant-window (1m) and decay-window (30m with half-life 10m) aggregates. Fast spikes should be evaluated but require corroboration over 10–30m for automated actions.

Decision recipes (examples):
1) Immediate automated throttle: if p99 latency > 2x baseline AND tail error rate > 0.5% in last 1m -> throttle new model to 25% of sentinel capacity and page steward.
2) Automatic rollback: if hallucination_score delta > 30% AND business-metric deviation (rerank F1) > 10% over 30m -> rollback. Requires steward confirmation within 10m else automated rollback triggers.
3) Cost gating: if billing.delta_pct > 15% sustained for 1h -> pause canary and notify finance/product.

Quick-sample diagnostics (commands to run):
- Metrics: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95), sum(errors) FROM metrics WHERE model=pilot_variant AND ts>now()-5m
- Traces: open traces filtered by span=runtime/infer and model=pilot_variant, sort by duration desc (for slow tail).
- Behavioral diff: run evaluation harness: python eval/harness.py --model pilot_variant --dataset sentinel_prompts --output diffs.json
- Sample responses: curl -H "X-Canary: true" -d @sample_request.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq '.response'

Pre-flight checklist (before enabling pilot-sentinel):
- [ ] Configured feature flag + traffic slice in Console with guardrail expiry time
- [ ] Instrumented sentinel metrics and traces (metric names above exist)
- [ ] Steward roster assigned and calendar invites sent
- [ ] Token budget set (max tokens/hour) and billing alert linked
- [ ] Automated throttle/rollback runbooks in place and tested in staging

Run-time checklist (daily/shift):
- [ ] Steward viewed dashboard during shift start
- [ ] No unresolved alerts older than 15m (or escalated)
- [ ] Run the 10-sample sanity sweep (script below) if any signal drift seen

Sanity-sweep script (sketch):
- pick 10 golden prompts from sentinel_prompts
- call pilot_variant with X-Canary header, call control model in parallel
- compute simple diffs: answer length ratio, semantic similarity (embedding cosine), hallucination heuristics -> write to gist and tag steward channel

Rollback vs throttle decision tree (short):
- Safety regression (hallucination, toxicity) -> immediate rollback unless can be mitigated by prompt filter; steward MUST confirm before re-enable
- Latency spike w/o errors -> throttle then investigate kernel/queue; if p99 remains high after 30m -> rollback
- Cost spike w/o quality change -> pause and ask for model config (quantize? batching?)

Communication & comms templates:
- Page template: [PILOT-SENTINEL] model=<name> issue=<latency|error|cost|quality> summary=<1-2 lines> link=<dashboard/gist>
- Slack channel: #pilot-sentinel (tag steward-oncall). Use thread for triage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to standardize hallucination_score across model families? (action: research team to propose unified heuristics by 2025-03-08)
- Can we add automated golden-prompt sampling at scale without costing as much as a live canary? (engineering exploration)
- Evaluate whether half-life 10m is optimal for noisy traffic — propose A/B on aggregation windows.

Appendix: quick links and references
- Canary dashboard template: /dashboards/pilot-sentinel-template (Confluence page above)
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Related runbooks: JIRA-5241 (rollout-ops), doc: /shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/release-needlepoint-ops-notebook.json

Revision history:
- 2025-02-18 A.Patel: initial draft and checklist
- 2025-02-25 L.Chen: added aggregation recipe and throttle rules
- 2025-03-01 M.González: steward rotation protocol, signal list edits

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep the pilot small. We want signal, not surface area.
- When in doubt, prefer rollback and re-introduce faster after investigation.
- Keep steward burden low: automate sampling and summary generation as soon as possible.

Unresolved snippets (copy here during triage):
- last alert snippet: "p99 latency 2.9s, p95 400ms, error rate 0.02%" (check infra queue)
- sample prompt id: sentinel-20250225-17

End of doc
